apps.name: static-landing

auth.description: Public marketing site; no authentication.

apps.name: nextjs-saas-dashboard
apps.title: Lumeo Analytics – SaaS dashboard (Next.js 15)
apps.description: Fictional product-analytics SaaS: marketing pages plus a role-protected dashboard and admin area. Auth is a jose-signed HS256 JWT in an httpOnly cookie, enforced by Next.js middleware.

env.name: AUTH_SECRET
env.description: HS256 secret used to sign/verify the session JWT. Falls back to the demo value when unset; set a long random string in real deployments.

env.name: PORT
env.description: HTTP port of the standalone server.

env.name: HOST
env.description: Bind address (npm start maps it to Next's HOSTNAME).

env.name: COOKIE_SECURE
env.description: Set to "true" behind HTTPS so the session cookie gets the Secure flag. Keep false for plain-HTTP smoke tests.

env.name: DATA_DIR
env.description: Directory holding db.json (auto-created and seeded on first request).

auth.description: Login (Server Action form or POST /api/login) verifies a bcryptjs hash and sets cookie `lumeo_session` = HS256 JWT (8h, httpOnly, SameSite=Lax). middleware.ts verifies it for /dashboard/* (any user) and /admin/* (role admin); unauthenticated -> 307 to /login?next=..., non-admin on /admin -> 403.

apps.persistence: JSON file at data/db.json (DATA_DIR), auto-created and seeded with 3 users + 8 projects on first request; role changes are written back to it.
apps.notes: Requires a writable DATA_DIR (Docker: mount a volume at /app/data). `npm start` runs the Next.js standalone server (.next/standalone/server.js) produced by `npm run build`; the build's postbuild step copies static assets into it. Smoke test: POST /api/login with JSON {email,password} using a cookie jar, then GET /dashboard (200) vs. without cookie (307 to /login). `npm audit` reports advisories only in Next's bundled postcss (transitive; fix requires Next 16).

env.description: Comma-separated origins WITH scheme (e.g. https://blog.example.com); required for form POSTs when served over HTTPS behind a proxy.

env.name: DJANGO_DB_PATH
env.description: SQLite file path; absolute or relative to the project root. Parent directory is created automatically. The Docker image sets /app/data/db.sqlite3.

env.name: PORT
env.description: Port gunicorn binds to (entrypoint.sh only).

env.name: GUNICORN_WORKERS
env.description: Number of gunicorn workers (entrypoint.sh only).

auth.description: Django contrib.auth session cookies (sessionid + csrftoken). /accounts/login/ POSTs a CSRF-protected form; /write/, /dashboard/ and post editing require a logged-in user; /admin/ requires is_staff. Logout is POST-only.

apps.persistence: SQLite file at data/db.sqlite3 (DJANGO_DB_PATH); Docker image stores it at /app/data (declared VOLUME). Created by `migrate`, seeded idempotently by `seed_demo` (entrypoint.sh runs both on every start).
apps.notes: Single container, no external services. entrypoint.sh runs migrate -> collectstatic -> seed_demo -> gunicorn on $PORT (8003). Mount a writable volume at /app/data to keep posts across restarts. When served over HTTPS via a reverse proxy set DJANGO_CSRF_TRUSTED_ORIGINS to the public origin, otherwise login/comment form POSTs fail CSRF checks. Static files are served by WhiteNoise from the same process (no separate static server needed). Requires Python 3.12+ locally (verified on 3.14; Docker image uses 3.12).

No cookies, no sessions.

apps.persistence: SQLite file at data/scribble.db (DATABASE_PATH); Docker image stores it at /app/data (declared VOLUME). Tables are created and demo data seeded automatically on first start (create_app), or explicitly with `flask --app app seed`.
apps.notes: Single container, no external services. Startup is safe with multiple gunicorn workers (concurrent create_all/seed is tolerated). The docs page loads swagger-ui-dist from cdn.jsdelivr.net at browser time; the API itself has no runtime network dependency. GET / redirects (302) to /docs. Mount a writable volume at /app/data to keep data across restarts.

apps.name: express-ejs-inventory
apps.title: Depot Ninety – warehouse inventory (Express 4 + EJS)
apps.description: Classic server-rendered multi-page app for a fictional warehouse: item CRUD with search/filters, a low-stock admin report, express-session cookies, hand-rolled CSRF tokens and a lowdb JSON store.

env.name: SESSION_SECRET
env.description: Secret that signs the express-session cookie. Falls back to the demo value (with a startup warning) when unset; set a long random string in real deployments.

env.name: PORT
env.description: HTTP port.

env.name: HOST
env.description: Bind address.

env.name: COOKIE_SECURE
env.description: Set "true" behind HTTPS so the session cookie gets the Secure flag (keep false for plain-HTTP smoke tests).

env.name: TRUST_PROXY
env.description: Set "true" behind a reverse proxy (Express trust proxy = 1).

env.name: DATA_DIR
env.description: Directory holding inventory.json (auto-created and seeded on first start).

auth.description: express-session (in-memory MemoryStore) with cookie `depot.sid`; passwords are bcryptjs hashes. Every state-changing POST must carry the `_csrf` field that matches the token stored in the session (scrape it from any rendered form, e.g. the login page). Unauthenticated page requests are redirected 302 to /login; /admin and item deletion require role admin (403 otherwise).

apps.persistence: lowdb JSON file at data/inventory.json (DATA_DIR), auto-created and seeded with 2 users, 3 categories and 15 items on first start. Sessions live in process memory and are lost on restart.
apps.notes: Needs a writable DATA_DIR (Docker: mount a volume at /app/data). Single-process only (MemoryStore); express-session prints a MemoryStore warning in production - expected for this demo. Tailwind is loaded from cdn.tailwindcss.com in the browser, so end users need internet access for styling (the server itself makes no outbound calls). Smoke test: GET /login with a cookie jar, scrape `name="_csrf" value="..."`, POST /login (form-urlencoded: _csrf, username, password) -> 302 to /items, then GET /items -> 200; GET /admin as clerk -> 403, as admin -> 200. `npm audit` reports 2 moderate advisories in Express 4's transitive `qs`; the fix would be Express 5.

apps.name: sveltekit-shop
apps.title: Terracotta Supply – plant-pot shop (SvelteKit 2 + Svelte 5)
apps.description: Fictional plant-pot e-commerce site: product catalogue, cookie-stored cart, checkout that writes orders to a JSON store, customer account area and an admin product CRUD, all built on SvelteKit form actions with a server-side cookie session resolved in hooks.server.ts.

env.name: ORIGIN
env.description: Public origin of the site (scheme://host[:port]) as browsers see it. SvelteKit rejects form-action POSTs whose Origin header differs from it (403), so set it to the real public URL (e.g. https://shop.example.com) for anything other than localhost access. `npm start`/the image default it to http://localhost:3012 with a warning.

env.name: PORT
env.description: HTTP port of the adapter-node server.

env.name: HOST
env.description: Bind address.

env.name: COOKIE_SECURE
env.description: Set "true" behind HTTPS so session/cart cookies get the Secure flag (keep false for plain-HTTP smoke tests).

env.name: DATA_DIR
env.description: Directory holding users.json, sessions.json, products.json and orders.json (auto-created and seeded on first request).

auth.description: Cookie `tc_session` holds an opaque id looked up in a server-side Map (persisted to data/sessions.json, 7-day TTL) by hooks.server.ts, which sets event.locals.user. Login/register/logout are SvelteKit form actions (POST /login?/login, /register?/register, /logout). Route-group layouts enforce access: (account) redirects anonymous users 303 to /login?next=..., (admin) additionally requires role admin (403 otherwise). Passwords are bcryptjs hashes.

apps.persistence: JSON files in data/ (DATA_DIR): users.json, products.json (10 seeded pots), orders.json, sessions.json - created and seeded on first request, rewritten atomically on change. The cart lives client-side in the `tc_cart` cookie.
apps.notes: Needs a writable DATA_DIR (Docker: mount a volume at /app/data). Set ORIGIN to the public URL or every form submission (login included) fails with 403 'Cross-site POST form submissions are forbidden'. For curl smoke tests send `Origin: http://localhost:3012` and `Accept: text/html` on action POSTs: e.g. `curl -c jar -H 'Origin: http://localhost:3012' -H 'Accept: text/html' -X POST 'http://localhost:3012/login?/login' -d 'email=shopper@terracotta.shop&password=Shop123!'` -> 303, then `curl -b jar http://localhost:3012/account` -> 200 (without the cookie: 303 to /login). Without `Accept: text/html` SvelteKit answers action POSTs with 200 + JSON ({"type":"redirect"|"failure",...}). Actions without fields (checkout, logout) still need a form-encoded body (`-d ''`), otherwise 415. `npm audit` lists 3 low advisories in transitive dev tooling only.

apps.persistence: SQLite file inside the api container at /app/data/orbit.db on the named volume orbit-api-data (created and seeded automatically at API startup). The web service is stateless static files.
apps.notes: services: api (FastAPI/uvicorn, container port 8015, published 8015, healthcheck /healthz) and web (nginx:1.27-alpine serving the built SPA, container port 5015, published 5015, depends_on api healthy). The web container's nginx.conf proxies /api/ -> http://api:8015/ (prefix stripped) and provides history-API fallback to index.html, so only port 5015 needs to be exposed publicly; 8015 is optional for direct API access/Swagger. VITE_API_URL is a BUILD-TIME arg for the web image - rebuild the web image to change it. Local (non-Docker) run needs two processes: uvicorn on 8015 and Vite on 5015 with VITE_API_URL=http://localhost:8015 and CORS_ORIGINS including http://localhost:5015.

apps.name: go-gin-url-shortener
apps.title: Kısa.link – URL Shortener
apps.description: A Go/Gin URL shortener with click statistics, a JSON API and an HTTP Basic Auth protected admin panel, persisted in a pure-Go SQLite database and compiled into a single static binary.

env.name: PORT
env.description: HTTP port to listen on

env.name: BASE_URL
env.description: Public base URL used to build short links (set to the deployed origin, no trailing slash)

env.name: ADMIN_USER
env.description: HTTP Basic Auth username for /admin

env.name: ADMIN_PASS
env.description: HTTP Basic Auth password for /admin (demo value; override in real deployments)

env.name: DB_PATH
env.description: SQLite database file path; directory is created if missing (Docker image sets /data/kisa.db)

env.name: GIN_MODE
env.description: Gin mode: debug | release | test (Docker image sets release)

auth.description: Public shortening, redirect, stats and JSON API. The /admin area is protected by HTTP Basic Auth (gin.BasicAuth) with credentials from ADMIN_USER / ADMIN_PASS; unauthenticated requests get 401 with a WWW-Authenticate header.

apps.persistence: sqlite file at data/kisa.db (WAL mode; /data/kisa.db inside the container) – schema migrated and 5 demo links seeded on first start
apps.notes: Single static binary, no CGO needed. go.mod requires go >= 1.25 (Go toolchains >= 1.21 auto-download it). Container runs as uid 65532 (distroless nonroot): a named volume mounted at /data works out of the box, but a host bind-mount directory must be writable by uid 65532 (chown 65532:65532 ./data). Set BASE_URL to the externally visible origin so generated short links are correct.

apps.name: spring-boot-library
apps.title: Kütüphane Plus – Library Lending System
apps.description: A Spring Boot 3 library lending system with a public catalogue, member borrowing/returns and a librarian admin area, using Spring Security form login with server-side sessions and CSRF, Thymeleaf views and a file-based H2 database.

env.name: PORT
env.description: HTTP port (server.port)

env.name: DB_PATH
env.description: H2 database file prefix without extension; H2 creates <DB_PATH>.mv.db (Docker image sets /app/data/library)

env.name: SPRING_PROFILES_ACTIVE
env.description: Set to 'prod' to hide stack traces/messages in error pages (Docker image sets prod). H2 console is disabled in every profile.

env.name: JAVA_OPTS
env.description: Extra JVM flags (Docker entrypoint only)

auth.description: Spring Security form login (POST /login with username/password/_csrf) backed by a BCrypt UserDetailsService over the members table; JSESSIONID cookie session, CSRF token required on every POST, roles ROLE_ADMIN and ROLE_MEMBER enforced by requestMatchers (/admin/** hasRole ADMIN, /my/** and /loans/** authenticated). 403 renders a custom page.

apps.persistence: H2 file database at ./data/library.mv.db (DB_PATH; /app/data inside the container) – schema managed by Hibernate ddl-auto=update, seeded with 10 books, 2 users and 3 loans when the members table is empty
apps.notes: Java/Maven are not required on the host when using Docker (multi-stage build compiles inside maven:3.9-eclipse-temurin-21). Without Docker, JDK 21 is required and ./mvnw downloads Maven 3.9.16 on first use (needs network). First Maven build downloads ~120 MB of dependencies. Container runs as non-root user 'app'; mount a writable volume at /app/data. Startup takes ~8-20 s before /actuator/health returns 200, so give the healthcheck a start period.

apps.name: dotnet-razor-helpdesk
apps.title: Masaüstü Destek – IT Helpdesk Ticketing
apps.description: An ASP.NET Core 10 Razor Pages helpdesk where requesters open and follow tickets and agents/admins triage them, using ASP.NET Core Identity cookie authentication with three roles, EF Core migrations on SQLite and folder-convention authorization.

env.name: ASPNETCORE_URLS
env.description: Listen address(es); the app falls back to 0.0.0.0:8018 when unset (Docker image sets http://+:8018)

env.name: ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT
env.description: Development shows developer exception pages; Production uses the /Error page

env.name: ConnectionStrings__Default
env.description: SQLite connection string; the directory is created automatically and also holds the Data Protection keys (data/keys). Docker image sets Data Source=/app/data/helpdesk.db

auth.description: ASP.NET Core Identity with cookie authentication (cookie 'masaustu.auth', 8 h sliding). Custom Razor Pages for /Account/Login, /Account/Logout (POST only) and /Account/Register using SignInManager/UserManager – no scaffolded Identity UI. Roles Admin / Agent / Requester; /Admin folder protected by the AdminOnly policy convention (AuthorizeFolder) plus [Authorize(Roles="Admin")] on /Admin/Users; /Tickets requires a signed-in user and requesters only see/open their own tickets; status changes and assignment are Agent/Admin only. Antiforgery tokens on every POST. Unauthenticated → 302 /Account/Login, forbidden → 302 /AccessDenied (renders with HTTP 403).

apps.persistence: SQLite file at data/helpdesk.db (WAL mode; /app/data/helpdesk.db in the container) created by EF Core migrations (Database.Migrate() at startup) and seeded with 3 roles, 3 users, 4 categories and 10 tickets when empty; Data Protection keys are stored in data/keys so cookies survive restarts
apps.notes: Requires the .NET 10 SDK to build (runtime image mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/aspnet:10.0). Container runs as the non-root 'app' user (uid 1654); mount a writable volume at /app/data (named volume works out of the box, a bind mount must be writable by uid 1654). Run the app from a directory where wwwroot/ is available (publish output or project dir) – static CSS is served from wwwroot. Self-registration is open and creates Requester accounts.

apps.name: vue-spa-kanban
apps.title: Flowboard — Vue 3 kanban SPA
apps.description: Client-only kanban board (Vue 3 + Vite 6 + Vue Router 4 history mode + Pinia + Tailwind 4) with mock login and role-guarded routes. Board and session live in localStorage; there is no backend at all.

auth.description: Client-side only. Login compares against hard-coded users in src/mocks/users.ts and stores a fake token + user in localStorage['flowboard.auth']. Vue Router beforeEach guards enforce requiresAuth (/board, /settings) and requiresAdmin (/admin) with redirect to /login?redirect=<path>. Nothing is enforced server-side.

apps.persistence: browser localStorage only: flowboard.auth (session) and flowboard.board (columns + cards, seeded from src/mocks/board.ts on first visit)
apps.notes: HTML5 history mode: the host MUST rewrite unknown paths to /index.html with status 200 (nginx: try_files $uri $uri/ /index.html — see nginx.conf; Netlify: public/_redirects; Vercel: vercel.json). Every route including /board/c-3 must return index.html; the SPA renders its own 404 view. Port 5019 is only the Vite dev server (npm run dev), not needed in production. `npm run build` runs vue-tsc type-checking first; use `npm run build-only` to skip it.

apps.name: bun-elysia-htmx-polls
apps.title: Pulsebox - live polls
apps.description: Live polling app on the Bun runtime with Elysia, server-side JSX templates and HTMX partial swaps (votes and auto-refreshing results). Passwordless email-OTP login with a signed session cookie and an env-defined admin list; bun:sqlite storage.

env.name: APP_ENV
env.description: Anything other than `production` enables GET /dev/last-code and shows the OTP on the verify page. Set `production` for real deployments.

env.name: PORT
env.description: HTTP port.

env.name: SESSION_SECRET
env.description: HMAC-SHA256 key that signs the session cookie. The demo default works but is insecure; a warning is logged in production.

env.name: ADMIN_EMAILS
env.description: Comma-separated emails that receive the admin role after logging in.

env.name: DB_PATH
env.description: SQLite database file; created and seeded with 3 polls on first start.

auth.description: Email + 6-digit one-time code (10 min, single use). No mail provider: the code is printed to the server log and, when APP_ENV != production, returned by GET /dev/last-code?email=... and shown on the verify page. Success sets an HMAC-signed httpOnly cookie `pb_session` (7 days). Admin = email listed in ADMIN_EMAILS.

credentials.password: (no password - fetch the OTP from the server log or GET /dev/last-code?email=admin@pulsebox.app)

apps.persistence: sqlite file via bun:sqlite at DB_PATH (image: /app/data/pulsebox.sqlite on the /app/data volume); schema created and 3 demo polls seeded automatically when the polls table is empty
apps.notes: Runs as the non-root `bun` user (uid 1000): a bind-mounted data directory must be writable by that uid (named volumes are fine). There is no email delivery - to log in, read the OTP from `docker logs` or call /dev/last-code (non-production only). Set APP_ENV=production and a real SESSION_SECRET for anything public. HTMX is loaded from unpkg CDN; no build step.

apps.name: react-dotnet-kitchen-display
apps.title: Ocakbaşı KDS – Restaurant Kitchen Display System
apps.description: A real-time restaurant kitchen display: customers order from a table page, the kitchen works a live queue and a public big-screen board follows every order. One ASP.NET Core 10 Minimal API container hosts the React build from wwwroot, pushes updates over a SignalR WebSocket hub and authenticates staff with short-lived JWTs plus a rotating httpOnly refresh cookie.
apps.install: cd web && npm ci && cd ../api && dotnet restore
apps.build: cd web && npm run build && cd ../api && dotnet publish -c Release -o out /p:UseAppHost=false
apps.dev: cd api && dotnet run  # terminal 2: cd web && npm run dev (Vite on 5021, proxies /api, /hubs (ws), /healthz to 8021)

env.name: ASPNETCORE_URLS
env.description: Listen address; the code falls back to 0.0.0.0:8021 when neither ASPNETCORE_URLS nor --urls is given (Docker image sets http://+:8021)

env.name: ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT
env.description: Production by default; Development only adds verbose logging

env.name: JWT_SECRET
env.description: HS256 signing key for access tokens, minimum 32 characters (startup fails otherwise). The default is a DEMO value and is logged as a warning; set a private one in production

env.name: JWT_ISSUER
env.description: Issuer and audience claim of the access tokens

env.name: ACCESS_TOKEN_MINUTES
env.description: Access token lifetime (the SPA refreshes one minute before expiry)

env.name: REFRESH_TOKEN_DAYS
env.description: Lifetime of the kds_refresh cookie / stored refresh token

env.name: COOKIE_SECURE
env.description: Set true when served over HTTPS so the kds_refresh cookie carries the Secure flag

env.name: TRUST_PROXY_HEADERS
env.description: Set true behind a reverse proxy: honours X-Forwarded-For/X-Forwarded-Proto from any proxy so rate limiting sees the real client IP

env.name: CORS_ORIGINS
env.description: Comma-separated browser origins allowed to call the API with credentials; only needed for the Vite dev server – production is same-origin

env.name: ORDERS_PER_MINUTE
env.description: Fixed-window rate limit for POST /api/orders per client IP (429 with Retry-After when exceeded)

env.name: ConnectionStrings__Default
env.description: SQLite connection string; the directory is created automatically. Docker image sets Data Source=/app/data/kds.db

auth.description: Hybrid JWT: POST /api/auth/login {email,password} returns a 15-minute HS256 access token (claims sub/email/role, sent as Authorization: Bearer) and sets an httpOnly SameSite=Strict cookie 'kds_refresh' (path /api/auth, 7 days, stored as a SHA-256 hash). POST /api/auth/refresh rotates the cookie and issues a new access token (reusing a rotated cookie revokes every session of that user); POST /api/auth/logout revokes it. The SPA keeps the access token in memory only and restores sessions by calling /refresh on load. Roles Admin and Staff enforced by the policies AdminOnly and StaffOrAdmin; missing/invalid token -> 401 problem+json with WWW-Authenticate: Bearer, wrong role -> 403 problem+json. Passwords are hashed with Microsoft.AspNetCore.Identity.PasswordHasher (no full Identity). The SignalR hub /hubs/orders is anonymous and read-only (events orderCreated, orderUpdated, menuChanged). Customer endpoints are public; POST /api/orders and POST /api/auth/login are rate limited per IP.

apps.persistence: SQLite file at api/data/kds.db locally (WAL mode, -shm/-wal side files) or /app/data/kds.db on the /app/data volume in Docker; schema comes from the committed EF Core migration (Database.Migrate() at startup) and an idempotent seeder adds 2 users, 12 menu items and 6 orders when the tables are empty. Refresh tokens are rows in the same database.
apps.notes: Single container / single port: the API serves the React build from wwwroot (SPA fallback for every path except /api/* and /hubs/*, which return JSON 404s). Real-time updates use SignalR over WebSockets, so any reverse proxy MUST forward Upgrade/Connection headers for /hubs/ (nginx: proxy_http_version 1.1; proxy_set_header Upgrade $http_upgrade; proxy_set_header Connection "upgrade"); without it the client falls back to long polling. Behind HTTPS set COOKIE_SECURE=true, and behind a proxy set TRUST_PROXY_HEADERS=true so the 10/min order limit is per real client IP instead of per proxy. The container runs as the non-root 'app' user (uid 1654) and needs a writable /app/data (a named volume works out of the box; a bind mount must be writable by uid 1654). The start command runs the published DLL from api/ so the database lands in api/data; the web root is resolved automatically (cwd/wwwroot, then <dll dir>/wwwroot, then ../web/dist). Requires the .NET 10 SDK to build and Node >= 20.19 for the web build; port 5021 is only the Vite dev server and is not exposed in production. JWT_SECRET default is a demo value – override it.
